item.description:
Sign-in

  • GitHub sign-in works again. 0.2.0 shipped with the ID of a retired OAuth app; Harbor now uses its new app, which needs no client secret.

CLI and polish

  • `harborcli local --root` with a folder that doesn't exist is an error, not "No repositories found".
  • Errors and help name the command `harborcli`.
  • The "stats are being generated" notice says Harbor, not a leftover name.

First signed release.

Sign-in and security

  • Sign in to GitHub with a one-time code at github.com/login/device. Harbor no longer ships an OAuth client secret. Your own OAuth app (e.g. GitHub Enterprise) still signs in through the browser.
  • Signing in can no longer get stuck on "Signing in…"; you can cancel it, and sign-in errors now show in the menu.
  • OAuth token responses are no longer written to the diagnostics log.
  • A GitHub Enterprise host typed without `https://` (`ghe.example.com`) now works; an unusable host shows an error instead of quietly signing in to github.com.

Azure DevOps

  • Work-item queries are valid WIQL: "is one of" filters, area and iteration paths with backslashes, tag filters, and the first condition of a query.
  • Project filters now filter by project, and "last N days" / stale-item queries use N instead of today.
  • Commit change counts show up.

CLI

  • `harborcli` help and messages use the Harbor name throughout.

Look

  • New app icon: a mooring bollard with a yellow line made fast around it.

Security

  • Every secret (GitHub tokens, OAuth app credentials, Azure DevOps PATs, GitLab tokens) is kept in the macOS Keychain through one store, local to your Mac and never synced to iCloud.
  • Listing Azure DevOps organizations no longer fails when a PAT is saved.
  • All known dependency vulnerabilities fixed.

Local Git

  • A missing git or a folder that isn't a repository is reported as such, not as "uncommitted changes".

Packaging

  • Developer ID signed, notarized, hardened runtime; Sparkle updates from github.com/sriinnu/harbor; Homebrew cask `sriinnu/tap/harbor` installs the app and the `harborcli` command.
